titleEn: Earth’s rocks have a missing layer spanning up to a billion years. We finally know where it went
titleZh: 地球岩层中缺失的十亿年：科学家追踪它们去了哪里
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Imagine opening a history book and finding several chapters torn out. This was what geologists looking into the rock records of Earth’s past discovered on several continents in the 1870s.
paragraphs.zh: 想象一下，打开一本历史书，发现有几章被撕掉了，这是地质学家在19世纪70年代在几个大陆上研究地球过去的岩石记录时发现的。

paragraphs.en: They dubbed it the Great Unconformity. Where layers of rock often stack up in a steady sequence from oldest to youngest, in many places around the world there is a gap of hundreds of millions of years.
paragraphs.zh: 他们称之为“大不整合面”，岩石层通常以稳定的顺序从最古老的到最年轻的堆积起来，在世界上许多地方，这是一个数亿年的差距。

paragraphs.en: For 150 years, nobody has known what erased those missing chapters. In new research published today in Nature, we finally provide an explanation: deep processes inside Earth lifted some continents high above the sea, where their surfaces were scoured down by the grinding movement of enormous sheets of ice.
paragraphs.zh: 150年来，没有人知道是什么抹去了这些缺失的章节。在今天发表在《自然》杂志上的一项新研究中，我们终于提供了一个解释：地球内部的深层过程将一些大陆抬升到海面之上，它们的表面被巨大的冰层的研磨运动冲刷下来。

paragraphs.en: The Great Unconformity
paragraphs.zh: 大不一致

paragraphs.en: Layers of rock often stack up in chronological order, with the oldest at the bottom and the youngest at the top.
paragraphs.zh: 岩石层通常按时间顺序堆叠，最古老的在底部，最年轻的在顶部。

paragraphs.en: Yet in some places, such as the Grand Canyon in North America, you can touch rock layers from two different ages, hundreds of millions of years apart. A flat layer of sedimentary rock, about 540 million years old or younger, rests directly atop a crystalline “basement” up to two billion years old.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，在某些地方，比如北美的大峡谷，你可以触摸到两个不同时代的岩层，它们相隔数亿年。一层平坦的沉积岩，大约5.4亿年或更年轻，直接位于一个结晶的“基底”上，最多有20亿年的历史。

paragraphs.en: Somewhere in between, a considerable chunk (up to a quarter) of Earth’s history has simply vanished.
paragraphs.zh: 在这两者之间的某个地方，地球历史的相当一部分（高达四分之一）已经消失了。

paragraphs.en: Important things happened in that time. The sedimentary layers on the younger side of the Great Unconformity appear at the same time as a huge diversification in the forms of life on Earth. This is the so-called Cambrian explosion, which began around 540 million years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 在这段时间里发生了一些重要的事情。在大不整合面较年轻一侧的沉积层出现的同时，地球上的生命形式也发生了巨大的变化。这就是所谓的寒武纪大爆发，大约开始于5.4亿年前。

paragraphs.en: Scientists have speculated entire continents were eroded during the Great Unconformity, which may have altered the chemical balance of seawater and allowed animal life to flourish.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家们推测，在大不整合运动期间，整个大陆都被侵蚀了，这可能改变了海水的化学平衡，使动物生命得以繁衍。

paragraphs.en: The puzzle of missing rock
paragraphs.zh: 失落的岩石之谜

paragraphs.en: Geologists have found evidence of the Great Unconformity throughout North America and parts of northern China, as well as beneath younger rocks in northern Europe. Yet its origin has remained a puzzle.
paragraphs.zh: 地质学家在整个北美和中国北方部分地区以及北方较年轻的岩石下发现了大不整合的证据。但它的起源仍然是一个谜。

paragraphs.en: Some scientists have argued it was caused by erosion by massive ice sheets during the Snowball Earth period between 720 million years and 635 million years ago. Others have pointed to the reshuffling of continental blocks, mountain-building processes, heat-induced movement inside the Earth, volcanic activity, or global sea level change.
paragraphs.zh: 一些科学家认为，这是由7.2亿年至6.35亿年前的雪球地球时期的大规模冰盖侵蚀造成的。其他人则指出，大陆块的重新洗牌，造山过程，地球内部的热诱导运动，火山活动或全球海平面变化。

paragraphs.en: Testing these hypotheses has been a challenge because the primary evidence consists of missing rock. As a result, we need to work from what we already know to fill in the gaps.
paragraphs.zh: 验证这些假设一直是一个挑战，因为主要的证据包括缺失的岩石。因此，我们需要从我们已经知道的东西来填补空白。

paragraphs.en: How hot rock can move continents
paragraphs.zh: 热岩石如何移动大陆

paragraphs.en: We had a theory that the creation of the Great Unconformity might have been influenced by heat-driven motion in Earth’s mantle. The mantle is a 2,900-kilometre thick layer of hot solid rock that slowly moves over tens to hundreds of millions of years. Hot mantle rises from deep beneath and cold mantle sinks, pushing and pulling the surface above.
paragraphs.zh: 我们有一种理论认为，大不整合面的形成可能受到了地幔热驱动运动的影响。地幔是一层2,900公里厚的热固体岩石，在数千万至数亿年的时间里缓慢移动。热地幔从下面深处升起，冷地幔下沉，推动和拉动上面的表面。

paragraphs.en: This huge, slow movement can raise or lower the surface by hundreds of metres. Continents sit on top of the mantle and get pushed up and down by its motion.
paragraphs.zh: 这种巨大而缓慢的运动可以使地表升高或降低数百米。大陆位于地幔顶部，并被它的运动上下推动。

paragraphs.en: We used the Australian supercomputer Gadi to model how the movement of the mantle had affected continents over the past billion years.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用澳大利亚超级计算机Gadi来模拟地幔运动在过去十亿年中如何影响大陆。

paragraphs.en: Our results consistently showed that mantle convection caused ancient continental blocks Laurentia (which now makes up much of North America), Baltica (parts of northern Europe), and North China to be lifted up from around a billion years ago to 540 million years ago. Over the past 540 million years, they have been pulled downward.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究结果一致表明，地幔对流导致古老的大陆板块劳伦提斯（Laurentia，现在构成了北美的大部分地区）、波罗的海（Baltica，北方欧洲的一部分）和华北从大约10亿年前到5.4亿年前被抬升，在过去的5.4亿年里，它们被拉下。

paragraphs.en: This up-and-down movement is the ideal scenario for the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity. When these continental blocks were lifted up, we see the crystalline underlayer was at the surface – and the layers of sediment above were eroded away. Then when the blocks sank, new layers of sediment began to form, which are preserved in rock to this day.
paragraphs.zh: 这种上下运动是大不整合面形成和保存的理想场景。当这些大陆块体被抬升时，我们看到结晶底层位于地表--上面的沉积层被侵蚀掉了。然后当这些块体下沉时，新的沉积层开始形成，这些沉积层保存在岩石中直到今天。

paragraphs.en: Lifted continents scoured clean by ice
paragraphs.zh: 抬升的大陆被冰冲刷干净

paragraphs.en: Importantly, the uplift predicted by our models coincided with the Snowball Earth period. During this period, enormous ice sheets scraped over the surface of continents for tens of millions of years.
paragraphs.zh: 重要的是，我们的模型预测的隆起与雪球地球时期相吻合。在这一时期，巨大的冰盖在大陆表面刮了几千万年。

paragraphs.en: Glaciers and ice sheets are more efficient than rivers at eroding continents, even on gentle slopes. The ice sheets would have slowly slid downhill across the uplifted continents, eroding away everything in their path.
paragraphs.zh: 冰川和冰盖对大陆的侵蚀比河流更有效，即使是在平缓的斜坡上，冰盖也会沿着隆起的大陆缓慢下滑，侵蚀掉沿途的一切。

paragraphs.en: In contrast to Laurentia, Baltica and North China, we found that Australia and South America experienced only two cycles of uplift and subsidence from 900 million years ago. This scenario is not conducive to the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity – and indeed we see little evidence of it on these continents.
paragraphs.zh: 与劳伦提斯、波罗的海和中国北方相比，我们发现澳大利亚和南美洲从9亿年前开始只经历了两次隆升和沉降，这种情况不利于大不整合面的形成和保存--事实上，我们在这些大陆上几乎没有看到它的证据。

paragraphs.en: Our research suggests the missing pages in Earth’s geological archive may be due to slow mantle convection that gently lifted entire continents then made them subside over hundreds of millions of years.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究表明，地球地质档案中缺失的页面可能是由于缓慢的地幔对流，缓慢地抬升了整个大陆，然后使它们在数亿年内下沉。

paragraphs.en: In that sense, the Great Unconformity is the fingerprint of deep Earth processes. Forces deep beneath our feet have left planet-scale marks in the geological record, and shaped the environment in which complex life first evolved.
paragraphs.zh: 从这个意义上说，大不整合面是地球深部过程的指纹。我们脚下深处的力量在地质记录中留下了行星规模的痕迹，并塑造了复杂生命最初进化的环境。
